strings.name: Jamie Dimon
strings.summary: Jamie Dimon began at American Express and financial businesses associated with Sandy Weill, led Bank One and became JPMorgan Chase CEO in 2006. He participated in crisis-era acquisitions and bank integration, including expansion through the resolution of First Republic Bank in 2023. His influence in banking is accompanied by debate over risk controls and regulation; the London Whale trading loss and related penalties are important parts of assessing his management responsibilities.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach the 2023 First Republic resolution, with a November 2026 SEC certification corroborating living status and role. His CEO and chair terms began on 1 January 2006 and 1 January 2007 respectively. Institutional penalties are distinguished from personal liability.
strings.influence.rationale: Led JPMorgan Chase over many years, influencing global banking, responses to financial crises and regulatory debates.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BA, Tufts University (1978); MBA, Harvard Business School (1982)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Managing large banks over time
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: From Bank One to JPMorgan Chase, participated in major mergers, crisis acquisitions and the management of a diversified bank.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Risk and regulatory responsibilities
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Testified before Congress after the London Whale losses; the bank subsequently faced regulatory penalties for related control failures.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Acquires most First Republic assets
strings.timeline.event-01.text: In a regulatory resolution, JPMorgan Chase assumed all First Republic deposits and substantially all its assets, expanding the bank further.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Bank is penalized over the London Whale episode
strings.timeline.event-02.text: US and UK regulators penalized the bank for related control failures; this was institutional responsibility, not a personal criminal conviction of Dimon.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Testifies to the Senate about trading losses
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Answered questions following disclosure of major trading losses; the bank later reported approximately $6.2 billion in London Whale losses.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Participates in crisis-era acquisitions
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Led JPMorgan Chase through the acquisitions of Bear Stearns and Washington Mutual banking operations during the financial crisis.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes JPMorgan Chase chair
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Added the board chairmanship one year after becoming CEO, combining the two leadership roles.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes JPMorgan Chase CEO
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Moved from president and COO to chief executive of the diversified financial institution.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Joins JPMorgan Chase through a merger
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became president and COO of the combined company after Bank One merged with JPMorgan Chase.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Takes the helm of Bank One
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After leaving Citigroup, became Bank One chair and CEO, taking responsibility for its operations and turnaround.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Leaves Citigroup
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Briefly served as president of the newly combined Citigroup before departing after a falling-out with Weill.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Earns an MBA and joins American Express
strings.timeline.event-10.text: After Harvard Business School, worked for Weill and entered financial management and acquisitions.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Graduates from Tufts
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Completed undergraduate studies before consulting work and further business education.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in New York City
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in New York into a family connected with securities, later entering bank management.
